reads: the Bash command's text, this session's records directory and the other sessions' directories under the session root

cases.name: deny-cat-of-the-seats-notepad-by-absolute-path
cases.why: The Read tool is denied the seat's folder by the settings; a cat is the same read through the shell, and the operator wants a lane unable to see the seat's records (2026-10-16).

cases.name: deny-the-other-lanes-report-by-relative-path
cases.why: A path spelled from the worktree still names the other lane's folder: the root's name and the folder's name together are the tell.

cases.name: deny-a-write-into-the-seats-folder
cases.why: Reading and writing another session's records are the same trespass; the rule looks at the path, not the verb.

cases.name: deny-python-opening-the-seats-folder
cases.why: The path is matched in the command's text, whatever program reads it.

cases.name: allow-own-notepad
cases.why: A session's own records are its to read and write.

cases.name: allow-the-shared-roster
cases.why: The roster and the grants sit at the root, outside every session's folder; the rule names only the other sessions' folders.

cases.name: allow-the-seat-reading-a-lane
cases.why: The seat reads a lane's notepad when it compacts or reviews it. The entry does not run the rule for the seat (its roster row carries `seat`, or its records folder is named `seat`), so the rule itself sees no other folders; this case states the contract the entry keeps.

cases.name: allow-a-word-that-only-resembles-the-folder
cases.why: Only the root's own name followed by the folder's (draft/seat) or the absolute path matches; a bare folder name in prose does not.

cases.name: allow-when-the-host-separates-nothing
cases.why: A host that sets no HARNESS_RECORDS_DIR keeps every record at the root, and the rule has nothing to guard; silence, never a wrong refusal.
